subject.title: Stability, installer auth, runtime compatibility, and context-management improvements

question: How should maintainers split the remaining #86567 umbrella across dashboard auth persistence, Codex/OpenAI OAuth propagation, installer/runtime atomicity, and context/liveness defaults?
rationale: The remaining work changes credential persistence and propagation, upgrade behavior, package compatibility, and terminal session semantics, which are product and security-boundary choices rather than a safe one-shot repair.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Canonicals
options.body: Keep this issue as the coordinating umbrella and make each active subproblem own its security contract, owner boundary, and proof path.

options.title: Run One Coordinated Reliability Project
options.body: Treat the issue as a maintainer-led project spanning auth, installer, runtime, and context-management rather than ClawSweeper automation.

options.title: Close After Canonical Links
options.body: Close this umbrella only after maintainers designate narrower open items as the sole canonical trackers for every remaining acceptance criterion.

recommendation.title: Split Into Narrow Canonicals
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the coordinating umbrella and make each active subproblem own its security contract, owner boundary, and proof path.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle appears in the most relevant provider/auth docs, compaction/liveness, and partial final-turn fix history, making it the best available routing owner for the split decision.
